sections.heading: C — Sharing the Road
sections.markdown:
## C — Sharing the Road

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A101
Share the roadway courteously and communicate your position and intended movement to other users. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A101
Yield to people crossing in a marked crosswalk, including when traffic-control equipment is not operating. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A101
The manual’s safety guidance also directs yielding to pedestrians outside crosswalks and when your traffic signal is green. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A101
Stop completely for a pedestrian crossing with a guide dog or white cane. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A101
Do not pass a vehicle that has stopped or is slowing to yield to someone in a crosswalk. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A101
Yield to pedestrians when making a permitted turn on red. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A101
Watch for people beside parked or stopped vehicles, and check behind before backing in parking lots. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A101
Reduce speed near homes and playgrounds and be ready for children to emerge between parked cars. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A101
At a school crossing, stop and yield when directed by the crossing guard. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A101
Follow the reduced school-zone speed when warning lights flash or children are present outside. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A101
Before crossing a sidewalk, yield to pedestrians and cyclists using it. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A101
Exercise care to avoid striking pedestrians or cyclists regardless of other traffic rules. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A101
A bicycle is a vehicle, and its rider shares vehicle drivers’ road rights and responsibilities. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A102
Search deliberately for cyclists because their smaller, quieter vehicles lack the enclosure of a car. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A102
Expect differences in cycling skill and be ready for an unexpected swerve or turn. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A102
Yield where a bicycle path or bicycle lane crosses the road. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A102
Do not drive, stop or park in a bicycle lane except while entering or leaving a driveway or alley. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A102
When overtaking a cyclist, allow at least 3 feet between the cyclist and your vehicle’s right side. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A102
Slow for an approaching or overtaken cyclist and let the rider clear an intersection before you turn. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A102
Cyclists generally ride as far right as practical, but may choose another position when staying right is unsafe. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A102
On a lane too narrow for safe side-by-side travel, a cyclist may ride near its center. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A102
Check carefully for cyclists before a turn or opening a vehicle door. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A102
Give cyclists room to avoid potholes, debris and drain grates. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A102
Avoid suddenly slowing or stopping in front of a cyclist. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A102
In bad weather, increase both following room and passing room around cyclists. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A102
Reduce passing speed around cyclists, especially on a narrow road. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A103
Make a right turn near a cyclist only when it can be completed reasonably safely without interfering with lawful bicycle travel. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A103
Near a bicycle, sound the horn only for a collision risk, because the noise can startle the rider. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A103
Watch for a cyclist entering your lane, particularly a child riding from a sidewalk. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A103
Do not cut sharply across a cyclist’s path or force the rider off the road. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec10-F31 | anchor: A103
Although cyclists should travel with traffic, search for riders approaching from any direction. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec10-F32 | anchor: A103
Use added care near cyclists on wet pavement, sand or gravel. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec10-F33 | anchor: A103
A cyclist may need both hands on the bars and be unable to give a hand signal, so also watch head and shoulder checks. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec10-F34 | anchor: A103
Before opening a parked vehicle’s door, check the side and rear for bicycles. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec10-F35 | anchor: A103
The recommended Dutch reach opens the driver’s door with the right hand to encourage a look over the roadside shoulder. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec10-F36 | anchor: A103
Check for cyclists before backing and use extra care near schools or homes. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec10-F37 | anchor: A103
Maine does not require a bicycle-driving license, but traffic-rule violations by cyclists can bring fines. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec10-F38 | anchor: A104
A cyclist should practice before entering traffic and avoid traffic demands beyond their skill. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F39 | anchor: A104
Secure bicycle loads on a rack, in bicycle bags or on a trailer rather than hanging them from the bars or carrying them in the arms. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F40 | anchor: A104
The manual requires riders under 16 to wear helmets and use passenger seats while traveling on public ways. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F41 | anchor: A104
A cyclist continuing straight should use through traffic’s path rather than a right-turn-only lane. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F42 | anchor: A104
Cyclists should ride with traffic and avoid passing motorists on the right. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F43 | anchor: A104
The bicycle hazard-scan example looks 50 to 100 feet ahead for grates, potholes, tracks, puddles and debris. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F44 | anchor: A104
The manual advises crossing railway tracks at right angles while cycling. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F45 | anchor: A104
When cycling beside parked vehicles, the manual recommends 3 or 4 feet of door clearance. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F46 | anchor: A104
Ride a predictable line, avoid weaving between parked cars and check over the shoulder before changing position. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F47 | anchor: A104
Before a bicycle turn or lane change, look, signal and confirm the destination path is clear. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F48 | anchor: A104
For a vehicle-style left turn on a bicycle, check behind, signal and move left only when clear. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F49 | anchor: A104
A cyclist can instead make a left turn in two crossings, moving straight across, pulling aside and crossing left when safe. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F50 | anchor: A104
The manual’s bicycle night equipment includes a white front lamp visible at least 200 feet ahead and a red or amber rear lamp or reflector visible at least 200 feet behind. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F51 | anchor: A104
Reflective bicycle pedals are recommended unless reflective material is worn on the feet or ankles. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F52 | anchor: A104
Cyclists should allow extra stopping room in rain and carry suitable clothing and water. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F53 | anchor: A105
Motorcyclists share other drivers’ road rights and responsibilities; motorcycle licensing uses a separate manual. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-F54 | anchor: A105
Allow a motorcycle an entire lane, including when passing; do not squeeze alongside within the same lane. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

Misconceptions: cyclists can lawfully need the travel lane when riding beside a car would be unsafe. [A102]
Mnemonic: look, yield, leave room, communicate.
Glossary: a bicycle is a vehicle with road rights and duties. [A101]
Dynamic facts: legal coverage, equipment standards and undated traffic statistics remain review debt.

items.why: Yielding, lateral space, turning and door opening require different anticipatory checks.
Full lanes, blind areas and truck turning clearance require recognition and application.
Moving emergency response, police stops and stationary move-over duties are distinct.

corpus_stability.reason: Working assessment for the pinned Rev 4/24 snapshot: the frontmatter supplies one revision marker and this intake provides no evidence of more than annual revision. This is an inference for the fixed corpus, not a measured publication cadence; legal and administrative changes still require monitoring.
